issues.legal_issue: The exclusion of solatium and interest from compensation for compulsory acquisition under a highway-acquisition scheme violates equal protection when the exclusion distinguishes owners only by the public purpose or statute under which their land is acquired.
material_facts: The landowners’ property was compulsorily acquired for highway development under a special statutory scheme that did not provide solatium.
Landowners whose property was compulsorily acquired for other public purposes could receive solatium and interest under the general acquisition law.
The 1997 amendment’s stated aim was to expedite land acquisition and highway construction, and the court found that awarding solatium and interest did not impede that aim.
Solatium and interest had been available for highway acquisitions before the amendment and became available again under the later compensation framework.
issues.conclusion: The exclusion of solatium and interest was unconstitutional to that extent. The relevant provisions governing solatium and interest under the general acquisition law apply to acquisitions under the highway-acquisition scheme, and the exclusionary provision was declared unconstitutional to that extent.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not permit different compensation treatment for similarly situated owners merely because their land was acquired for a different public purpose or under a different acquisition statute, absent a rational basis for the distinction. Solatium compensates for the compulsory nature of acquisition and is part of compensation. The court relied on P. Vajravelu Mudaliar v. Special Deputy Collector for Land Acquisition (1965) 1 SCR 614, Nagpur Improvement Trust v. Vithal Rao (1973) 1 SCC 500, Balammal v. State of Madras (1969) 1 SCR 90, State of Kerala v. T.M. Peter (1980) 3 SCC 554, and Sunder v. Union of India (2001) 7 SCC 211.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_compulsory_a: A party challenges the constitutionality of the compensation treatment for compulsory acquisition.
predicates.owners_are_similarly_situated: The compared property owners are similarly situated with respect to the compulsory acquisition of their land.
predicates.compensation_difference_is_based_only_on: The owners receive different compensation treatment solely because their land was acquired for a different public purpose or under a different statute.
predicates.distinction_lacks_rational_relation_to_l: The different treatment has no rational relation to the object the legislation seeks to achieve.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns compulsory-acquisition compensation, a difference based only on acquisition purpose or statute is unconstitutional if similarly situated owners are treated differently without a rational connection to the legislative object, and the excluded compensation components must be paid.

issues.legal_issue: A law that expedites acquisition does not receive constitutional protection for excluding compensation components unless the exclusion has the required connection to distributing community resources and is essential to that purpose.
material_facts: The stated object of the amendment was to expedite the acquisition process and reduce delays in highway projects.
The amendment’s stated object was not the distribution of community resources.
The court found that excluding solatium and interest was not necessary to expedite acquisition.
issues.conclusion: Article 31-C did not protect the exclusion of solatium and interest from review under Article 14.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-C protection requires a direct and rational nexus between the law and Article 39(b), and protection extends only to provisions basically and essentially necessary to give effect to that directive principle. The court relied on Sanjeev Coke Manufacturing Company v. Bharat Coking Coal Ltd. (1983) 1 SCR 1000, State of Maharashtra v. Basantibai Mohanlal Khetan (1986) 2 SCC 516, Assam Sillimanite Ltd. v. Union of India 1991 Supp 3 SCR 273, Dr K.R. Lakshmanan v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996) 2 SCC 226, Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India 1981 (1) SCR 206, Maharashtra State Electricity Board v. Thana Electric Supply Co. (1989) 3 SCC 616, and Akadasi Padhan v. State of Orissa 1963 Supp (2) SCR 691.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_law_claiming: A constitutional challenge concerns a law said to implement a directive principle.
predicates.law_object_is_process_expedition: The law is intended to speed up or simplify a process rather than distribute community resources.
predicates.excluded_compensation_is_not_essential_t: The exclusion of compensation is not basically and essentially necessary to achieve the law’s object.

issues.definition: A law said to implement a directive principle is not shielded from equal-protection review when its object is process expedition and the challenged compensation exclusion is not essential to that object.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation for acquired user or easement rights does not justify withholding solatium and interest from owners whose land is compulsorily acquired.
material_facts: The highway-acquisition scheme provided a fixed amount when a right of user or an easement was acquired.
The general acquisition law also allowed compensation claims for affected easement interests, subject to proof.

The court explained that the special scheme’s payment related to rights held by persons other than the owner when ownership itself was acquired, and did not create an additional payment to the owner for the same right.
issues.conclusion: The treatment of user and easement rights did not answer or justify the exclusion of solatium and interest.
issues.legal_principle: Compensation for an affected easement or user right is distinct from solatium and interest payable for compulsory acquisition of ownership. Under the general acquisition law, the court relied on sections 3(b), 9, and 31(1), which permit a person interested in an easement to claim compensation. The court also considered the special scheme’s provision for compensation for acquired user or easement rights.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_compensation_disp: The dispute concerns compensation arising from compulsory acquisition.
predicates.separate_compensation_is_provided_for_us: The acquisition scheme provides compensation for an affected user or easement right, subject to the applicable claim requirements.
predicates.ownership_is_compulsorily_acquired: The owner’s land or ownership interest is compulsorily acquired.

issues.definition: When ownership is compulsorily acquired, separate compensation for user or easement rights does not substitute for or justify withholding solatium or interest.
